entry.title: Pose: a pure-NumPy, chirality-aware, structural engine for building and manipulating the molecular structures of proteins, nucleic acids, and small organic molecules
entry.summary:
Molecular modelling protocols often cross several programs, each with its own formats, conventions, and installation, and few treat D-amino acids and other non-canonical residues consistently. This work presents Pose, a Python library whose only run-time dependency is NumPy. Pose builds polypeptides, including six non-canonical amino acids, and nucleic-acid duplexes from sequence, with letter case setting each residue's handedness, and reimplements three force fields (OpenFF Sage 2.3.0, AMBER ff19SB, and CHARMM36) and two score functions (Rosetta REF15 and AutoDock Vina) as readable array operations.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: T2G: fast and accurate transcriptome to genome BAM liftover for short and long read RNA sequencing
entry.summary:
Aligning RNA sequencing reads to the transcriptome rather than the genome recovers short and junction-spanning reads that genome alignment loses or misplaces, but it leaves the alignments in transcript coordinates, which genome browsers, variant callers and most annotation tools cannot use. Existing liftover tools translate between genome assemblies, and the few that reach transcript coordinates are tied to a single quantification model or assay type. Here we describe T2G, which converts complete BAM files from transcriptome to genome coordinates while keeping CIGAR strings, alignment tags and per-base RNA modification calls intact.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: G-ALN: a GPU-accelerated BWA-aln algorithm for palaeogenomics
entry.summary:
Abstract Summary: The most commonly used method to achieve optimal mapping for short and damaged ancient DNA (aDNA) reads is the BWA-aln algorithm with seeding disabled. However, this CPU-based algorithm is computationally demanding, as the aligner must tolerate mismatches and indels across the entire read. To improve alignment speed, we present G-ALN: a GPU implementation of the BWA-aln and indexing algorithms.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: GEO-BERT: A Retrieval augmented LLM Framework for Intelligent Dataset Retrieval from the Gene Expression Omnibus
entry.summary:
The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) is a commonly used data repository of high throughput gene expression and other functional genomics data. This platform is globally used by researchers for submitting experimental datasets, accessing these datasets for hypothesis validation, reusing them in data-driven research, generating ideas for new research directions. Despite global usage, searching and identifying relevant and usable datasets in GEO remains challenging with an underlying keyword based search system needing manual intervention for the retrieval of desired datasets.

entry.title: Combining RNA-seq and proteomics boosts sensitivity to detect differentially expressed genes by rpMeta
entry.summary:
Differential gene expression analysis is a powerful technique to characterize biological systems. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) are commonly identified by analysis of RNA sequencing datasets or mass spectrometry proteomics datasets. Increasingly, multi-omic studies include both RNA sequencing and proteomics from the same biospecimens.

entry.title: Fibres and glasses are competing material states in protein condensation
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03415-z Fibres are thought to emerge from a dense protein condensate ageing into a glassy state. It is now shown that protein fibres and glassy condensates may result from two competing ageing pathways.

entry.title: HDOCK-Multimer: improved structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating docking and combinatorial assembly
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01062-1 This study presents HDOCK-Multimer, a general framework for structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating ab initio docking and combinatorial assembly, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
